base_rate_triangulation._citation: One population (US organizations), one role per source: FBI IC3 data-breach complaints set the base rate, IRIS the floor. TEF = LEF ÷ susceptibility.

base_rate_lef._method: IC3 recipe on US organizations: US data-breach complaints per year × under-reporting ÷ US firms in the revenue tier × the tier's share of victims.
base_rate_lef._n_us_note: FBI IC3 2025 report, complaints by crime type: Data Breach 3,963 (defined as computer intrusion to acquire confidential or secure information; separate from Ransomware and from Personal Data Breach, which counts individuals).
base_rate_lef._underreporting_note: Low and mode measured on ransomware: IC3 2025 Ransomware complaints 3,611 ÷ US ransomware victims (3,971 leak-site victims × under-reporting 1.33 / 1.46 / 1.75, ransomware.json) = IC3 filing rate 0.68 / 0.62 / 0.52; multiplier = 1 ÷ that. High 3.85 (judgment, labelled): data-breach victims file with IC3 half as often as ransomware victims at their lowest rate (1.925 × 2), since breaches go to regulators and the people affected rather than the FBI. Check: IC3's 3,963 data-breach complaints already exceed ITRC's 2,527 publicly notified US cyberattack compromises in 2024, which argues against a much larger multiplier.
base_rate_lef._tier_note: US firms per tier: Census SUSB 2022 (1–39 / 40–299 / 300–2,499 employees, as for ransomware). Victim shares: VCDB US incidents 2010–2024 with an external actor and confirmed data disclosure, ransomware excluded (1,086), employee classes split log-uniformly at 40, 300 and 2,500 employees (scripts/exfiltration_victim_shares.py): 0.230 / 0.206 / 0.215, and 0.349 for 2,500+ employees. VCDB is built from public reports, which over-represent large victims: measured directly, the 2,500+ tier (4,361 firms) gives about 0.6 loss events per firm-year, above IRIS 2022's all-incident upper bounds (17–29%), as Coveware did for ransomware. So from $1B the rate is the measured $100M–1B rate × IRIS's all-incident revenue multipliers relative to $100M–1B (IRIS 2025 Fig A2: 1.2 / 2.49 / 3.46 ÷ 0.8).
base_rate_lef._geography_note: The base rate counts US events over US firms, so the geography multiplier is relative to the US (US = 1.0).

vector_proportions._citation: DBIR 2026 vector shares, adjusted for exfiltration pattern (DBIR 2025 Espionage)

exfiltration_overall_share._citation: DBIR 2026 espionage pattern ~8% of breaches; IRIS does not separate exfiltration. Judgment anchor.

exfiltration_sector_shares._citation: No exfiltration-specific sector data. All null: the tool uses the IRIS 2025 all-incident sector multiplier (Figure A1) once.

exfiltration_revenue_shares._citation: No exfiltration-specific revenue breakdown available. Uses all-incident shares from IRIS 2025.

exfiltration_revenue_prob_gte2._citation: Not available from IRIS for exfiltration specifically. All null — tool falls back to overall floor.

credential_tempo._citation: Ransomware credential tempo scaled by the exfiltration-to-ransomware claim ratio: NetDiligence Cyber Claims Study 2025, Figure 51 (N=10,402 claims, 2020-2024): hacker 15%, ransomware 26% (verified against the PDF 2026-10-24).
credential_tempo._derivation: campaigns/month = ransomware [1,000, 2,000, 3,000] × 0.15/0.26 = [577, 1,154, 1,731]; credential_proportion = this scenario's credential vector share; addressable population as for ransomware (global, the same campaign markets). Bias: insured claims only, and 'hacker' is the closest NetDiligence cause to non-ransomware data theft.

exploitation_scanning._citation: GreyNoise-derived scanning telemetry. Exfiltration uses same scanning infrastructure as ransomware for initial access.
exploitation_scanning.grn_malicious_rate_note: Shared with ransomware: the GreyNoise IP-level malicious rate describes scanning, not the scenario; the scenario enters through ransomware_proportion_of_scanning and PoA.
exploitation_scanning.poa_ransomware_note: Lower than ransomware — exfiltration actors are more selective.
exploitation_scanning.ransomware_proportion_note: Exfiltration-motivated scanning is a smaller share than ransomware-motivated.
